subject: Dedicated pool: burst-surge plan & region selection for Quanta Bio
messages:
From: Alan Santos <alan.santos@quantabio.com>

Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia.m@quantabio.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool burst window questions

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We are finalizing our internal runbooks and have two items that will affect the Dedicated pool sizing and autoscale policy:

- Peak inference windows (we see large bursts between 10:00-12:00 PT and 18:00-20:00 PT)
- Regional preference: we need primary capacity in us-west-2 and a DR pool in us-east-1 (for latency and compliance reasons)

Two specific asks: can Redwood support a warm-burst pool (prewarmed nodes for short spikes) and a hard cap for overall GPUs to control budget spikes? Also, please confirm what the failover latency looks like if us-west-2 is overloaded and we reroute to us-east-1.

Attaching a short SOC2 excerpt and our simplified VPC diagram for context.

Alan
Alan Santos
VP, Engineering — Quanta Bio
alan.santos@quantabio.com

Attachments: quanta_soc2_summary.pdf, network_vpc_diagram.png
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Alan Santos <alan.santos@quantabio.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool burst window questions

Alan —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Short answers up front: yes, we can provision a warm-burst pool and enforce a configurable hard GPU cap. Failover latency to a secondary region depends on routing/policy you choose; typical cold failover adds ~250-500ms to initial request latency due to cross-region routing plus model cold-starts if there is no warm cache in the target region. With warm-burst nodes in the DR region, you should be in the ~75-150ms range for most requests.

Proposed plan:
- Provision primary Dedicated pool in us-west-2 sized for sustained baseline (we recommend baseline = 60% of your 95th percentile steady-state).
- Configure a warm-burst mini-pool in us-west-2 sized for expected spike headroom (~20-30 GPUs) with fast scale-up triggers (event-based + predictive schedule for your 10:00-12:00 and 18:00-20:00 windows).
- Reserve a cold-standby pool in us-east-1 under the hard cap. Optionally we can keep a small warm pool there if you require sub-200ms failover SLAs.
- Hard cap enforced at the tenant routing layer; finance can be notified by alert when consumption approaches 85% of cap.

Karthik, copying you for sizing and autoscale knobs; Monica — can you pick this up in the implementation plan and own the kickoff with Quanta next week? I’ll coordinate the technical call.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Alan Santos <alan.santos@quantabio.com>, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 14:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool burst window questions

Alan / Vivek —

Quick technical notes to complement Vivek's proposal:

- Warm-burst implementation: we use a tiny prewarmed KV cache + 1-2 prewarmed model replicas per shard to ensure sub-200ms cold-starts for typical prompts. For large context lengths we recommend keeping an extra replica per shard.
- Autoscale triggers: combination of token-throughput thresholds (sustained 75% utilization for 30s) and scheduled scale events for the two daily windows you mentioned. We'll also enable proactive pre-scaling using historical traffic curves if Quanta agrees to share the last 14 days of traffic samples.
- Hard cap: implemented in the routing layer with an enforced token-bucket for allocation. If cap is reached we can degrade to a smaller model variant or route noncritical requests to standby region depending on policy.

Open items for Quanta to confirm:
1) do you want warm nodes in us-east-1 or is cold-standby acceptable?
2) acceptable budget headroom (% of cap) for automated notifications (default is 85%).
3) do you want automatic fallback to smaller model variants, or would you prefer a hard reject + 429 to surface capacity constraints to callers?

I can prepare an ops runbook and parameterized autoscale JSON once we lock these.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Martinez <sofia.m@quantabio.com>

Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:49:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool burst window questions

Thanks — quick answers from our infra/security team:

1) We need a small warm pool in us-east-1 (at least 4 GPUs) because some of our regulated workloads require sub-200ms legislative responses during peak windows.
2) Notifications at 80% are preferred. Finance will want an early heads-up so we can throttle nonessential batch jobs.
3) Prefer fallback to a smaller verified model variant (same output schema) rather than returning 429s.

We attached the SOC2 excerpt and a minimal VPC diagram in the first email — let us know if you need more specifics on network egress rules or private link endpoints.

Sofia Martinez
Cloud Infrastructure Lead — Quanta Bio
